## ⚠️ 前提过时检查

The card's line numbers (`:57` `:62` `:67`) are plugin-grid's copy read on an earlier `origin/main`. ⭐ The dev re-derives both copies on the current tip and says whether they are still identical to each other — 「two shared helpers」 is itself a claim that can rot.

## ⭐ What this card actually is

Two test doubles spread a `records` array **only** when the request carries `recordIds`, so a single-`recordId` request comes back without `record.visible` and `useRecordEditable` **fails open** through them — ⛔ against the helpers' own docblock, in the two files most likely to be copied.

⇒ ⚠️ this is a **test-double** defect, which is the sharp kind: it makes real suites green about a permission decision that would not hold in production. ⭐ The deliverable therefore includes the question 「**what was passing because of this, and does it still pass once the double tells the truth?**」 — ⛔ if fixing the double reddens a suite, that red is the finding and it stops and reports rather than tuning the double back.

## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9902 is ready + auto-merge, with `Fixes #9813`. ⭐ The defect was **latent**, and a **THIRD copy** the fence did not know about had already settled the shape.

### ⭐ The two readings the card marked NOT MEASURED, both delivered

**① Were the two copies still identical?** ⛔ **No** — and the card's md5 pair reproduces **exactly** on the current tip (`2650630e…` / `3cd7e361…`, 73 vs 76 lines). ⭐ But the card printed the hashes and ⛔ did **not** diff them; this run did: **every byte of the difference is docblock prose** (a different card citation, different wrapping, one extra paragraph, two sentences plugin-view omits). The **executable code was byte-identical before the change and is byte-identical after it** ⇒ one patch genuinely applied twice, and the repair did ⛔ not have to diverge between them.

**② What was passing because of the wrong double?** ⭐ **Nothing.** Both helpers were instrumented to log every request they answered, and every file importing either was run: **75 explain calls, all batched `recordIds`, ZERO singular** — with those **75 as the lit control in the same command**.

⚠️ ⭐ **And the first run of that probe returned zero for BOTH sides.** That was the probe, ⛔ not the tree: **this repo's configured vitest reporter prints no console output at all**, so an instrumented run needs `--reporter=default`. ⇒ ⛔ without the control, a confident zero built on a **dead instrument** would have been published. That is 说明 ⑯'s sibling — the instrument was not a grep this time, and the control caught it just the same.

⇒ the stop-and-report condition the dispatch armed (「if fixing the double reddens a suite, that red is the finding」) **never fired**: the same 13 importing files are **13 passed / 152 tests**, identical to before. ⛔ The double was never tuned back, because it never had to be.

### ⭐⭐ A THIRD copy exists, and it was ALREADY CORRECT

`packages/test-support/src/record-security-explain-double.ts`. Re-read at source by this seat on `origin/main` `c1f039a6`: its docblock at `:38-39` states the shape, and `:120-122` implements it —

```ts
recordIds
  ? { records: recordIds.map((recordId) => ({ recordId, visible: true })) }
  : { record: { visible: true } },
```

⇒ ⭐ **the repair needed no design decision — it adopts a shape already settled in this tree.**

⚠️ And **how it was found is the transferable part**: the dev enumerated every tracked path matching `double` case-insensitively — **5 hits out of 8040 tracked paths** (seat-verified), which is narrow *and* lit. ⛔ A bare `explainDouble` grep would have returned a confident 「exactly two」. ⇒ ⭐ when a card says 「there are exactly N of these」, **enumerate by the concept, ⛔ not by the identifier**.

### The ablations, and a green that was PREDICTED before the run

Two legs, one per copy: deleting the singular spread from **plugin-grid**'s reddens plugin-grid's pin (DENY leg) while plugin-view's stays green, and vice versa. ⇒ ⛔ neither pin is reading the other's copy. Both mutations proven by blob hash, both restores by hash equality **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`.

⭐ **The PERMIT leg stayed GREEN under both mutations, and the pin file says so in advance:** `useRecordEditable` initialises its verdict to `true` and its fail-open leaves it there, so **a permitted answer and an absent one are the same value at that read site**. ⇒ the PERMIT leg is labelled a direction **CONTROL**, ⛔ not a pin. Predicting a green before the run and then labelling it correctly is the practice this lane has been asking for all shift.

⚠️ One more honesty item, reported rather than quietly replaced: a hand control-byte scan's **first control was a DUD** — a grep character range including LF can never match — and it was re-drawn with a deliberately dirty file firing in the **same command**.

### `Fixes`, and why this seat accepts it

⭐ The dev chose a closing keyword here having refused one on a sibling card two hours ago, and the ground is measured: the repair, **both** NOT-MEASURED readings and the pin all land here, and ⛔ no real fail-open survives in `useRecordEditable` — that hook's fail-open is **deliberate, documented on the hook, and already pinned by its own suite** for the non-OK, throwing and no-verdict cases. ⇒ nothing about production permissions is implied and nothing needs a separate fence. **Accepted.**

Changeset: **empty frontmatter**, and measured rather than assumed — both packages publish `dist`, both build tsconfigs exclude `__tests__`, and after building each package `installExplainDouble` has **zero** hits anywhere under either `dist` while a published symbol of the same package hits **in the same command**. It matches the convention `.changeset/explain-double-wire-shape-7996.md` already set for the sibling repair.

### ⛔ Three things recorded and deliberately NOT carded

- **Consolidating the three doubles onto `@object-ui/test-support`'s** is a real simplification — and a **13-file** change with a different helper API (no call log, no echoed `object`/`operation`/`allowed`/`layers`). ⚠️ ⛔ It is ⛔ not one of the three filing classes, and the honest answer to 「which PR will touch this file?」 is **none today**. ⇒ recorded here, ⛔ not carded. 承接者:无.
- **plugin-view's docblock says there is 「no repo convention for importing another package's test-only files across a workspace boundary」** — ⚠️ falsified by the tree: **two `plugin-designer` suites already import plugin-grid's copy by relative path**. ⛔ But it was false **before** this branch, it lives in a test file that ⛔ does not publish, and no author reads it. ⇒ ⛔ not carded, and named here so it is findable. ⚠️ Recorded as a tension, ⛔ not as a clean call: this lane's headline defect all shift has been a false sentence, and the only thing separating this one from a card is that **nothing publishes it**.
- **`AccessExplainPanel`** (app-shell) is the **second** production reader of the singular `decision.record.visible` — the card asked whether others existed. It imports neither double ⇒ unaffected.

### ⚠️ One thing the fence got wrong, and the dev handled it right

The declared surface said 「two shared helpers」. There are **three**. ⇒ ⛔ the seat's fence encoded the card's count as fact. The dev measured, found the third, left it untouched (it was already correct) and **reported** — which is exactly the shape 说明 ㉗ asks for: *a dispatch inherits the claims of the card it quotes*, and the remedy is the dev's reading, not the dispatch's confidence.
